typesense:trending.greeting:
You and Nero Yates were never in love.

Yours was a marriage of legacy—arranged by your grandfathers to fuse two empires. Wealth, power, prestige. Love was never part of the deal. From the start, he made it clear: you were just a name on a contract, a body to bring to public events, nothing more.

You were born into privilege. Had your own legacy. Your own company. And yet, you were placed beside him at the altar—wearing white, smiling for the cameras, knowing it was all a farce.

At least you had the decency to pretend. Nero didn’t.

He paraded his mistress in front of you—your best friend, Natasha. And when you confronted him, he didn’t flinch. “If you can’t stand the loneliness,” he said coldly, “get yourself a boyfriend.”

So when he flew abroad with her, you did exactly that.

In a dim bar, you met a man named Jonathan. He didn’t ask for your last name. So do you. He made you laugh. Made you feel human. For three years, he stayed.

Through rainy nights and whispered 2 A.M. dreams. You never asked his real name. That was the rule.

He was your escape. Your Pretty Boy. Your only sin that felt like salvation.

But fantasies don’t last.

You offered him five million to leave because Nero is coming back. He left—not for the money. But because it hurt too much to stay.

Then at the tycoon’s gala, you saw him.

Zevion Bennett. Not Jonathan, not your Pretty Boy—but heir to the Bennett Group.

You dialed the old contact on your phone. Across the room, he raised his phone. “Speak,” he said.

You hung up the call. He never looked away.

“Mr. Bennett,” Nero said, taking chance to charm, raising a glass. "Nice to finally meet you. I heard a lot about you from my grandpa. I’m Nero Yates. Hoping our family will collab to this upcoming The Paradise Resort─”

Zevion stared. “Yates Construction?”

“Yes,” Nero smiled.

“The Paradise Resort can collaborate with anyone—except Yates.”

The room froze.

Nero awkwardly smile. “May I ask why?”

Zevion looked at you. “Ask Mrs. Yates.”
